source_context_translations.translation: He practices a teaching without words; the myriad things arise and he does not refuse them, he gives birth to them and does not possess them, acts and does not rely on them,
accomplishes the work and does not dwell on it.
It is precisely because he does not dwell on it that it does not leave him.

If the worthy are not valued, the people will not contend; if hard-to-get goods are not prized, the people will not become thieves; if things that arouse desire are not shown, the people's hearts will not be in disorder.
Therefore, in the sage's governance, he empties their hearts and fills their bellies,

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To utter words or express something verbally.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often plain and direct, without necessarily implying formal speech.
Sentence Translations (English): A gentleman does not speak of profit.
I want to speak of it.
The Master speaks and keeps faith.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Language or spoken expression, especially the act or content of speaking rather than writing.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage it contrasts with silent action, so it points to verbal instruction or expression.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To instruct or train someone in knowledge or conduct.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can range from formal instruction to moral guidance.
Sentence Translations (English): The teacher instructs him in ritual.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The act of guiding or instructing others, especially by setting an example or imparting principles.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is the noncoercive Daoist mode of instruction, not schooling in a narrow institutional sense.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To perform an action or cause something to be made or done.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A very broad verb whose object or context determines the specific action.
Sentence Translations (English): The people all put forth labor.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To come into being or begin to occur, especially of natural things or processes.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It describes spontaneous emergence rather than deliberate human action.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; likely earlier Laozi layer as transmitted in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Refers to a place or situation previously mentioned.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often points back to an already named setting rather than introducing a new one.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A locative-consequential adverb meaning 'there' or 'thereupon,' marking the place or point at which something occurs.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it links the arising of things with the manner of response, not a concrete place-name use.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; likely earlier Laozi layer as transmitted in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Spoken or written words considered as a verbal expression.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can refer to the wording itself, often in elevated or literary usage.
Sentence Translations (English): The words fail to convey the meaning.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To reject, evade, or withhold acknowledgment or acceptance.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means not to disown or evade what has come forth, rather than polite refusal in later prose.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; likely earlier Laozi layer as transmitted in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To grasp firmly or keep in one's control.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often implies clinging to support or advantage.
Sentence Translations (English): He grasps it and relies on it.
He relies on his sword as he goes.
People become arrogant by relying on strength.
Do not cling to a single corner.
additional_senses.Translation (English): to hold in the hand; hold fast to

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To take support or assurance from something, or to lean on it as a basis for action.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): The sense here is not mere trust in an emotional sense, but dependence on one's own power or merit.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; likely earlier Laozi layer as transmitted in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Something brought to completion with favorable result.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often refers to a completed outcome or accomplishment.
Sentence Translations (English): The great achievement is now complete.
Achievement and fame may be attained.
Success lies in not giving up.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A completed accomplishment, deed, or productive result, especially one credited to someone.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is the result of effective action, not 'merit' as moral worth alone.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; likely earlier Laozi layer as transmitted in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A negative answer or denial used independently or in contrastive expressions.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Common in terse replies or emphatic negation.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A negative adverb denying or prohibiting the following verb.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A concise literary negative, often used in fixed or elevated phrasing.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A place where one lives or stays.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Usually concrete and locational.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To reside in, keep, or hold a place, status, or possession as one's own.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means to claim or hold onto the achieved result, not simply physical residence.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; likely earlier Laozi layer as transmitted in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): An adult male or husband, depending on context.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Commonly means a male person or spouse.
Sentence Translations (English): One man can hold the pass.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A sentence-initial particle introducing an explanatory or emphatic statement.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It frames the following clause as an explanatory conclusion or general remark.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; likely earlier Laozi layer as transmitted in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To regard, treat, or take something as something else.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often introduces a judgment or classification.
Sentence Translations (English): Under Heaven, virtue is taken as the root.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks exclusiveness or limitation to the following statement.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It narrows the explanation to a single reason or condition.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; likely earlier Laozi layer as transmitted in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To take something away or cause it to be absent.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often transitive, with a thing being eliminated or stripped away.
Sentence Translations (English): Cast off evil and follow good.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To leave, disappear, or be removed from a place or condition.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means not being lost or removed after achievement, not a casual 'go' verb.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; likely earlier Laozi layer as transmitted in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates continuation or persistence of a state.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Marks something as continuing up to the present or a later point.
Sentence Translations (English): The rain has not yet stopped.
The troops have not yet returned.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To prize, honor, or place importance on something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means to elevate social value or esteem, not the temporal adverb 'still.'
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; likely earlier Laozi layer as transmitted in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Having moral or practical excellence.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Describes a person or quality as deserving esteem.
Sentence Translations (English): He is worthy and not arrogant.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person judged morally capable, talented, or admirable.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it refers to socially prominent worthies whose elevation can provoke competition.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person sent on a mission or with a message.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often denotes one dispatched by authority.
Sentence Translations (English): He dispatched an envoy to inquire.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To bring about, induce, or let someone do something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage it introduces a causative effect on people's behavior.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Refers to ordinary people as a collective, or in some contexts the people of a region.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can also function in compounds or as a collective label for subjects.
Sentence Translations (English): The people must not be deceived.
Putting the people at peace comes first.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The common population or subjects as a collective social body.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Refers to the populace in contrast with rulers or sages.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To engage in verbal disagreement or debate.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often indicates contention in speech or claims.
Sentence Translations (English): There is no benefit in disputing.
The crowd all vied to speak.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To compete, quarrel, or struggle against another for precedence or advantage.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means social competition or rivalry, not a mere argument in the abstract.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Having high value or being rare and costly.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Describes price or intrinsic preciousness.
Sentence Translations (English): When goods are dear, the people are burdened.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To regard something as important, precious, or desirable.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means assigning worth or desirability to rare goods.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A state or condition of being hard to do or endure.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can refer to trouble, danger, or an adverse situation.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Not easy to obtain, accomplish, or endure.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it modifies goods that are hard to get, stressing scarcity.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates capability or possibility.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often appears in modal expressions of ability or feasibility.
Sentence Translations (English): With insufficient strength, one cannot obtain it.
This matter can be brought to completion.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To acquire, receive, or come to have something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it refers to the goods being obtained with difficulty, not to moral 'virtue.'
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To buy and sell or exchange goods.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A commercial sense that appears in economic or administrative prose.
Sentence Translations (English): He barters for it with silk.
He does not peddle his words.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Valuable items, property, or commodities.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it points to prized material goods, especially marketable wealth.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To take property unlawfully.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can also mean to pilfer or rob, depending on context.
Sentence Translations (English): He entered at night and stole.
He does not dare steal food.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person who steals or robs.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it denotes the kind of criminal behavior that social desire and greed may produce.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To show oneself or come into view.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Same character in the common passive/intransitive reading meaning something becomes visible.
Sentence Translations (English): The sun appears in the east.
Good and evil are both seen.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To look at, notice, or become aware of something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means not setting visible before the people, so that desire is not aroused.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The seat of thought, feeling, intention, or moral disposition.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can refer to cognition, emotion, or intention together.
Sentence Translations (English): Settle the heart and keep to the Way.
If the heart is upright, it is clear.
It is seen in his heart.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The inward faculty of thought, feeling, and intention in the populace.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is the collective inner state of the people, not an individual psychological term.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A state in which things are not ordered or controlled.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often refers to political or social turmoil.
Sentence Translations (English): All under heaven is in great disorder.
Long disorder must eventually be set right.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To be unsettled, confused, or thrown out of proper order.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it describes the people's hearts becoming internally unsettled, not merely external political chaos.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To exercise political control or bring order to a state or domain.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can imply ordering, administering, or bringing into good order.
Sentence Translations (English): He governs the people by virtue.
There is a Way to governing disorder.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The act or method of ruling and managing a state or people.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means the sage's mode of ruling, not a single administrative act.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Lacking contents, substance, or fullness.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can describe literal emptiness or figurative openness.
Sentence Translations (English): Its name is empty in vain.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To make something vacant, clear, or unoccupied.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means reducing inner fullness of desires or preconceptions, not merely 'false' or 'void.'
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The physical heart or the figurative center of something.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can be bodily, emotional, or central depending on context.
Sentence Translations (English): In the center there is no shame.
The heart is like still water.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The inner faculty of thought, feeling, intention, and moral awareness.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is the inner mental and affective center to be made empty.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Having substance, fullness, or being well supplied.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often contrasts with empty or虚, and may describe a state of abundance or firmness.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To put substance into something so that it is no longer empty or lacking.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it expresses satisfying bodily needs or supplying what is lacking.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The organ or seat of digestion and appetite.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can overlap with 'belly' but is often more specifically digestive.
Sentence Translations (English): When full, the stomach is at ease.
There is illness in the abdomen.
He travels on an empty stomach.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The body part below the chest that contains the stomach and related organs.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it stands for bodily nourishment and material sufficiency rather than mere anatomy.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text transmitted with Wang Bi commentary
